page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-3xL4 is a GPU-accelerated virtual server configured on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 16 shared vCPUs and 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.0 GB of RAM per core. The server is equipped with three NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, providing a total of 72 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance, requiring external storage attachment for data persistence.

The hardware profile presents specific architectural tradeoffs. While the provision of three NVIDIA L4 GPUs offers substantial parallel processing capabilities and a large VRAM pool, the 16 vCPUs use a shared allocation model. This shared CPU configuration may introduce resource contention under sustained, non-GPU compute loads, making the instance less optimal for CPU-bound tasks. However, this resource distribution provides a cost-efficient entry point for multi-GPU workloads, as users do not pay for dedicated high-core-count CPU allocations when the primary bottleneck is GPU memory or parallel execution.

This server configuration is designed for workloads that heavily leverage GPU acceleration and require significant system memory but have moderate CPU demands. Suitable use cases include machine learning model inference, medium-scale deep learning training, parallel data processing, and GPU-accelerated rendering tasks.
